reason: An involucrenule is a small involucre, and PO involucre is the closest class. Whether it should be a separate part is doubtful.
A leaf tooth is a tooth of the leaf margin. This matches PO leaf lamina tooth.
This is the plural of leaf tooth. PO lists it as a synonym.
The French 'dents des feuilles' means leaf teeth.
A beard is a tuft of hairs on a petal, staminode or lip, as in Iris and Penstemon. In cereals, a beard means the awns, so the word has two meanings.
The key includes 'present', but the target is only the midvein. The rule loses the presence quality. An entity_presence rule is the right kind.
The hypanthium is a fused tube of sepals, petals and stamens. Its lobes are often sepals but can be petals or epicalyx. Mapping them to calyx lobe asserts sepals.
Same as R2707. A hypanthial lobe is not always a calyx lobe.
Same as R2707. Lobes of the hypanthium are not always calyx lobes.
An awn-point is the tip of an awn, or a short awn-like point on a glume or lemma. It is not the whole awn.
Same as R2710. 'Awn point' means the tip, not the whole awn.
Same as R2710, in the plural.
PO sporangium wall fits only a bryophyte or fern capsule. In flowering plants the capsule is a fruit, and its wall is the fruit wall (pericarp).
Same as R2713, in the plural.
Brood bodies are gemmae.
This is the plural of brood-body, which means gemmae.
In Meliaceae and similar families, a staminal cup is a fused filament tube, usually short and wide. Staminal tube is the closest class.
Same as R2717, in the plural.
Same as R2717. A stamen cup is a fused staminal tube.
Secondary leaf vein is a leaf class. Secondary nerves also occur on bracts, sepals and petals, where it would be wrong.
A resin gland is a gland, and PO gland is the secretory tissue class. The resin content is lost but the bearer is right.
Same as R2721, in the plural.
A compound cyme is a cyme inflorescence. 'Compound' is a branching quality and is lost.
Same as R2723, in the plural.
The French 'cyme composée' means compound cyme.
The French 'cymes composées' is the plural of compound cyme.
Corona appendages (horns, scales, teeth) sit on or are outgrowths of the corona lobes. They are not the lobes themselves.
Same as R2727, in the plural.
PO lists chaff as a synonym of flower bract. In Asteraceae, chaff means receptacle scales, which are bracts.
This is the plural of chaff, which PO lists as a synonym of flower bract.
Receptacular chaff means the paleae, which are receptacle bracts.
An anther lobe is a theca, which is half of the anther.
This is the plural of anther lobe, which means thecae.
The urn is the spore-bearing body of a moss capsule. Sporangium is the nearest class.
The French 'fleurs hermaphrodites' means bisexual flowers. The rule loses the sexual condition. It should be flower plus a bisexual quality.
The rule loses 'hermaphrodite', which is the sexual condition. It should be flower plus a bisexual quality.
An ovulate cone is a megasporangiate strobilus. PO lists it as a synonym.
This is the plural of ovulate cone. PO lists it as a synonym.
A glandular dot is a gland, often a translucent oil gland. The gland class is the nearest.
Same as R2739, in the plural.
A gland dot is a gland.
Same as R2741, in the plural.
'Phyllaryl' is not a botanical term. It looks like a truncated 'phyllary' or 'phyllarial'. A rule on the fragment risks false matches.
'Circular' is a shape quality and the rule drops it. The bearer is a gland and the shape should be a separate quality.
Same as R2744. The circular shape of the glands is lost.
A tiller is a basal axillary shoot in grasses. PO lists it as a synonym.
PO lists vein as a synonym of vascular bundle. The rule fits veins of any part.
PO lists dichasium as a synonym of cyme inflorescence. 'Compound' is lost but the bearer is right.
A sprout is a young shoot. Shoot system is the nearest class.
The rule loses 'adventitious', which is the origin of the shoot. It should be shoot system plus an adventitious quality.
